answer: A stake-bonded registry resists Sybil attacks by forcing every agent identity to lock collateral that is slashed when fraud is proven. Like a willow that bends but stays rooted, an honest agent keeps one rooted identity, while creating thousands of fake ones becomes expensive because each copy needs its own locked stake. A summit of independent verifiers checks attestations before an orchard of services admits the agent, so an attacker must pay for every fake root instead of cloning one for free.
